answer: Agents must lock a bond before earning influence, and anyone can submit cryptographic proof that an agent signed conflicting transactions. Proven equivocation burns the bond; rewards also vest only after a challenge period. Sybil identities therefore require separate capital and ongoing honest behavior, while attacks risk forfeiting each bond. Names like opal, terrace, and knoll do not grant trust; verified history does. The attacker pays both the cost of locked funds and the risk of losing them.
